incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High error rate on /auth/token and elevated 502s from gateway in eu-west-1. Trigger: 3 consecutive 5m windows > 8% errors.
robert (oncall): acked. pulling up dashboard now. any customer reports? :phone:
alex (support): we have 4 tickets from customers in EU reporting auth failures since ~08:12 UTC. severity looks like login/token exchange errors.
sarah (eng-sre): looking at infra metrics — cache miss rate for auth-session namespace spiked 09:11 UTC, RedisCloud cluster rc-auth-eu showing degraded replication lag and CPU saturation.
maya (infra): confirmed. RedisCloud console shows degraded nodes and increased evictions. RC incident page lists ongoing maintenance for that cluster (incident RC-8421).
jin (eng-runtime): when cache misses spike, our rate limiter falls back to datastore checks and we have thundering writes to the DB which is causing upstream 502s. we need to reduce pressure to DB and re-enable local fallback immediately.
robert (oncall): runbook says: auth-cache failure -> enable in-memory local cache fallback, throttle auth token endpoints, and flip feature flag to use conservative token TTLs. i'll start handoff to sarah in 5.
sarah (eng-sre): i'm on it. first step: set rate limiter to fail-open for unknowns? that might allow high load. i'd prefer to enable local memcached pool and apply stricter leaky-bucket limits to heavy clients.
jin (eng-runtime): agree with local pool. command to enable local cache on auth pod group:
```bash
kubectl -n auth scale deployment/auth-local-cache --replicas=2
kubectl -n auth set env deploy/auth-service LOCAL_CACHE_ENABLED=true LOCAL_CACHE_TTL=60
```
robert (oncall): run those cmds, jin? i can monitor errors and rollback if needed.
jin (eng-runtime): running now, tailing logs.
[2m--- 09:22 UTC ---
jin (eng-runtime): local cache enabled on 3 pods. initial logs show reduced DB hits for token validation.
robert (oncall): nice. now throttling: reducing global auth token rate limit from 100r/s -> 40r/s to protect DB and downstream. applying config change via config-service.
sarah (eng-sre): deployed rate limit delta. policy: authenticated clients keep 60% of previous quota, anonymous endpoints 25%.
alex (support): updating tickets: "We observed an external caching provider (Redis Cloud) degradation affecting login/token flows in EU. We've applied local cache fallback and tightened rate limits to mitigate impact. Investigating upstream provider incident (RC-8421)."
pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to robert (oncall) and sarah (eng-sre). Escalation timeout set to 15m.
maya (infra): pinging RedisCloud support — opened ticket RC-8421 with provider reference ID 7f3b2. They responded: "We are investigating elevated CPU and replication lag, mitigation in progress."
robert (oncall): quick customer impact estimate?
sarah (eng-sre): based on traffic split, ~2.4% of total token exchanges in EU returned 5xx during peak. Affected customers are primarily EU tenants behind high-concurrency flows. No data loss.
robert (oncall): severity set to SEV-2 (partial degradation, business impact on EU auth). posting to status.redwood.io?
alex (support): posting now. status note: "Partial Authentication Failures in EU - Mitigation in progress (local fallback and rate limit adjustments)."
[2m--- 09:29 UTC ---
jin (eng-runtime): we're seeing 75% reduction in DB auth query rate from auth pods. 5xx rate trending down.
sarah (eng-sre): keep provider ticket open, but maintain mitigations until provider declares stable. also capture logs for postmortem: `auth-cache-miss-2026-03-15` run.
robert (oncall): i'm going to hand off paged ownership to sarah for the next shift. sarah, want it?
sarah (eng-sre): taking it. i'll be primary for follow-ups with RedisCloud and will coordinate rollback of the fallbacks after provider is OK.
robert (oncall): documenting actions in incident tracker. commands run:
```text
- Enabled LOCAL_CACHE_ENABLED=true on auth-service (3 pods)
- Scaled auth-local-cache to 2 replicas
- Applied conservative rate limits to token endpoints via config-service
- Opened RedisCloud ticket RC-8421, provider ref 7f3b2
```
alex (support): customers updated and notified via support tickets and status page. queued customers flagged for follow-up when resolved.
maya (infra): follow-up ops task: consider adding a graceful degradation path in rate-limiter to avoid DB spikes when cache provider degrades. Filing RFC.
sarah (eng-sre): assign postmortem owner once incident closed. suggested owner: jin (eng-runtime) for runbook changes, maya for infra tweaks, alex for customer comms.
pagerduty-bot: Reminder: next escalation in 10m if not resolved.
[2m--- 09:32 UTC ---
jin (eng-runtime): provider response update: RedisCloud applied a config roll to reduce eviction churn. replication lag improving.
sarah (eng-sre): 5xxs down to baseline ~0.8%. I'll keep mitigations for 30 more minutes then test rollback of rate limits.
robert (oncall): thanks team. handing off full context to sarah. handing over: root cause likely third-party cache provider degradation causing auth cache misses -> DB pressure -> rate limiter overload -> customer auth failures. mitigation: local fallback + tight rate limits + provider engagement.
sarah (eng-sre): confirmed takeover. continuing to monitor. I'll update incident tracker and set follow-up tasks.
alex (support): noted. tagging affected customers for follow-up and potential credits if SLA hit.
incident-bot: Incident thread updated. Mark as active and assigned to sarah (eng-sre).
